title: Dev-Only Synthetic Data Migration, Backup, Restore, and Rollback Rehearsal Map
authorityBoundary: Lower authority than semantic contracts, ADRs, validators, runtime proof evidence, and the backup/restore and data-migration proof artefacts it binds. This map records dev-only synthetic rehearsal intent and binds existing on-disk proof; it MUST NOT upgrade readiness and MUST NOT be treated as canonical proof.
syntheticDataBoundary: Every rehearsal step operates exclusively on synthetic, generated tenant fixtures (deterministic UUID tenants and seeded rows) inside profile-gated local Compose or hermetic proof harnesses. No live, real, customer-originated, or environment-promoted records are read, written, backed up, or restored. All evidence is repository metadata and value-free observation only; this map runs no docker or compose itself and only binds evidence artefacts that already exist on disk.

steps.description: Rehearse applying the forward-only numbered migration chain (checksum-immutable, one transaction per file, migrated-state gate) against a synthetic Postgres substrate. No on-disk execution-proof artefact records this migration rehearsal in HEAD: the identity-schema migration contract and the relational-storage-and-migrations-and-rls contract are semantic definitions only, and the referenced migration SQL and migrations unit test are historical source lineage that is not present on disk in this repository.
steps.nextRung: Author a dev migration-runner execution proof that applies the numbered chain to synthetic Postgres, asserts checksum-immutability drift refusal and the migrated-state gate, and emits a collected value-free execution-proof artefact.

steps.description: Seed a synthetic multi-tenant dataset (deterministic UUID tenants and RLS-guarded rows) as the subject of backup and restore rehearsal. The db-rls-isolation composed proof seeds synthetic tenants and RLS boundary tables under the runtime application role, and the pgBackRest and backup-operations proofs run against synthetic single-tenant Postgres. No live or customer-originated records are used.

Rehearse rollback as the contracts define it: forward-fix migration or a guarded restore only after migration lineage is verified. No dedicated rollback-rehearsal execution-proof artefact exists on disk in HEAD; rollback semantics are described in the relational-storage-and-migrations-and-rls and backup-and-restore contracts but are not exercised by a collected proof.
steps.nextRung: Author a dev rollback-rehearsal proof that demonstrates forward-fix and guarded-restore-after-lineage-verification against synthetic data and emits a collected value-free artefact.

steps.description: Profile-gated local Compose rehearsal that creates a pgBackRest online full backup while synthetic Postgres is running with WAL archiving, and dispatches a deterministic scheduled second (diff) backup. The USF-223 execution-proof records onlineBackupExecuted, walArchiveObserved, and scheduledBackupOperationExecuted as bounded local proof.

Profile-gated local point-in-time restore rehearsal: restores the synthetic backup into an isolated volume and replays archived WAL to a restore point. The USF-223 execution-proof records pitrRestoreExecuted as bounded local proof.

Data-layer usability verification of the restored dataset that is stronger than command exit success: after WAL replay to the restore target the proof performs a read-back and verifies that the post-target mutation is absent, confirming the restored synthetic dataset reflects the expected point-in-time content. This is a content verification, not merely a zero exit code, and it does not claim product or application-level usability.

Negative-path rehearsal: with the source Postgres stopped and the backup repository made unavailable, the restore fails closed and aborts rather than fabricating success, recording safe reason code pgbackrest-repository-unavailable. The USF-223 execution-proof records sourceFailureScenarioExecuted and failClosedChecked, and the pgBackRest boundary records missing-repository fail-closed behaviour.

Verify backup-set integrity of the created pgBackRest artefacts. The execution-proof observes backup set count, full and diff backup types, and a successful restore replay, which implicitly exercises artefact usability, but no dedicated backup-artefact integrity or checksum verification is recorded, and the provider disposition matrix explicitly marks backup integrity verification as deferred.
steps.nextRung: Add an explicit pgBackRest backup-set integrity and checksum verification test rung against the synthetic repository and emit a collected value-free artefact.

steps.description: Safe teardown of the restore container, Compose project, named volumes, socket and archive directories, and temporary overrides in finally paths. The USF-223 execution-proof records cleanupAttempted and cleanupSucceeded, and the pgBackRest boundary records restore-container, compose-volume, and temp-directory cleanup.

Rehearse the retention, legal-hold, and residency boundary: retention tick honouring an active legal hold, and residency rejection of out-of-home-region writes. No collected execution-proof exists on disk in HEAD; the pitr-retention-legal-hold-data-residency contract proof is hermetic lineage only, and the provider disposition matrix records retentionProofPresent false and defers retention execution.
steps.nextRung: Author a dev retention-boundary proof that exercises the retention tick honouring an active legal hold and residency rejection against synthetic data, emitting a collected value-free artefact.

steps.description: Redaction and secret-exclusion boundary: proof output prohibits secrets, connection strings, tokens, stack traces, table values, backup artefacts, restore payloads, and WAL file names, emitting value-free structured evidence only. The USF-223 execution-proof records redactionChecked and secretExclusionChecked.

Value-free audit-shaped evidence for the backup and restore operations is captured in the proof result with no product audit-log claim. The USF-223 execution-proof records auditEvidenceCaptured, and the pgBackRest boundary records value-free audit-shaped evidence.

Telemetry-shaped evidence: structured JSON logging, span-like tracing correlation, and metric buckets (readiness attempts, backup set count, WAL archive count bucket, duration buckets, cleanup state) are recorded as value-free proof metadata with no live tracing or metrics backend claim. The USF-223 execution-proof records structuredLogEvidenceCaptured, tracingEvidenceCaptured, and metricEvidenceCaptured.

pgBackRest configured local proof boundary: maintained digest-pinned image, configured repository, created stanza, synthetic Postgres linkage, offline cold full backup, restore readback, readiness retry, bounded timeouts, teardown, and missing-repository fail-closed behaviour. Recorded by the USF-211 configured-proof boundary and its proof source.
